title: EO 14248: Trump Overhauls Elections, Bans Late Mail Ballots
synopsis: On March 25, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14248, 'Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections,' the most sweeping federal incursion into state election administration in modern history. The order mandated documentary proof of U.S. citizenship on all federal voter registration forms, directed DHS and DOGE to review every state's voter rolls using federal immigration databases, threatened to withhold Election Assistance Commission funding from states that accepted mail ballots received after Election Day, and directed the Attorney General to sue states that count such ballots. Voting rights experts immediately warned the order exceeded presidential authority and could disenfranchise millions of eligible voters — including elderly, rural, and low-income citizens who disproportionately rely on mail voting. Courts blocked key provisions, but enforcement actions continued through 2026.

By April 2026, the LDF joined more than 1,300 nonprofits opposing new Trump administration certification requirements for all federal grant recipients that would expose civil rights organizations to criminal liability for lawful DEI activities. In July 2026, the Department of Education proposed rules to formally rescind EAC program regulations entirely, with LDF calling it 'a coordinated effort to weaken civil rights infrastructure, impede desegregation, and make schools less safe and accessible for Black students.'

title: EO 14173 Revokes 60-Year-Old Affirmative Action Contracting Rule
synopsis: On January 21, 2025 — his second day in office — Trump signed Executive Order 14173, 'Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity,' which revoked Executive Order 11246, the 60-year-old rule signed by President Lyndon Johnson in 1965 requiring federal contractors to take affirmative action in hiring. The Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs was immediately ordered to 'cease and desist all investigative and enforcement activity' and to stop holding contractors responsible for workforce diversity. All pending compliance reviews — including hundreds of federal contractors — were administratively closed. Federal contractors were required to certify in every new contract that they 'do not operate any programs promoting DEI,' with false certifications subject to federal fraud liability. The Congressional Research Service noted the revocation altered legal protections for employees at every company holding a federal contract, covering tens of millions of American workers.

title: Due Process Stripped: Courthouse Arrests, Fired Judges, Expedited Removal Expanded
synopsis: Throughout 2025 the Trump administration systematically dismantled immigration due process via three parallel strategies. First, beginning in May 2025 ICE stationed plainclothes agents in immigration courthouse hallways; a government attorney would request dismissal of a pending case, the judge would comply, and the immigrant would immediately be arrested upon exiting the courtroom — placed on fast-track 'expedited removal' with no further hearing. Second, the administration fired dozens of immigration judges and Board of Immigration Appeals members, creating a backlog leaving 3.6 million pending cases in chaos. Third, Trump expanded expedited removal to all undocumented immigrants nationwide regardless of how long they had lived in the U.S., a power a federal judge in August 2025 temporarily blocked, writing the administration's argument that undocumented people are 'entitled to no process under the Fifth Amendment' was 'truly startling.' Trump told reporters: 'I hope we get cooperation from the courts, because we have thousands of people that are ready to go out and you can't have a trial for all of these people.'

title: Family Separation 2.0: 600 Children in Federal Shelters, Highest Since Records Began

Of the 320,000 ICE detention book-ins in FY2026, nearly 17,900 were of people who self-reported as parents of U.S.-citizen children — nearly double FY2024. A New York Times report from August 2025 documented a Russian family separated at JFK Airport where their 8-year-old son Maksim was sent to an unaccompanied minors shelter; the last contact was May 15, 2025. The average shelter stay for children grew to nearly six months, up from one month under Biden.

synopsis: Founded in 1961, the U.S. Agency for International Development was effectively shut down by July 1, 2025, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced on March 10, 2025 that 5,200 of its contracts had been canceled — over 80 percent of all USAID programs.
